column1: # tools/css/gen-css-tables.py: the places where the pin's own text is not taken as it stands. Columns: directive, scope
# (the property a type is nested in, or empty for a global type), name (a type's name without the angle brackets), reason.
# A line that names nothing the pin has fails generation (stale). Nothing else in the pin is edited: this file is the whole
# list of departures, and tests/test-css-registry.cpp reads the effect of each from the generated tables.
# ignore-grammar   the entry's `value` is not a definition (it is a prototype of the function in prose), and is dropped.
# nested-ignore    a type or function the pin nests inside a type, at-rule, descriptor or selector (scope: that container's name, as
#                  the pin spells it) is not taken as a global definition of the name, because the pin nests the name in
#                  several containers and they do not say the same thing.
# append-grammar   the served draft gives the type another alternative that the pin's entry lacks: the line (directive, scope, name, reason,
#                  text) appends `| text` to the grammar. Stale when the pin has no grammar or already has the text.
# replace-grammar  the pin's text of a type is not the served draft's: the line (directive, scope, name, reason, old text, new text) replaces
#                  the grammar, and is stale when the pin's grammar is not the old text (white space folded).
# replace-property-grammar  the pin's grammar of a property lacks a range the served draft gives it: the line (directive, scope (empty), name, reason, old
#                  text, new text) replaces the grammar, and is stale when the pin's grammar is not the old text (white space folded).
# append-longhand the pin's shorthand lacks a longhand that the served draft's shorthand names: the line (directive, scope (empty), name (the shorthand), reason, longhands)
#                  appends the longhands (one name, or several separated by a space) to the shorthand's list, which may be empty. Stale when the pin lists one of
#                  them already, or does not have the shorthand or the longhand.
# append-reset   the pin's shorthand does not list a property that the served draft says it resets: the line (directive, scope (empty), name (the shorthand), reason, properties)
#                  appends them (separated by a space) to the properties the shorthand resets. Stale when the pin lists one of them already, or does not have it.
# enum-from-values the pin defines the type only through the keyword values nested in its entry; the grammar is those
#                  keywords, in the pin's order, separated by `|`.
